evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學
evidence.field: 形義通解；《說文》與《廣韻》資料
evidence.text: The entry for 叚 reports bronze forms analyzed as 爪 + 又 with 石 as phonetic (the mouth portion of 石 simplified to two short strokes). It records Xu Shen’s gloss 借也, “borrow,” and cites bronze uses read as 嘏 “blessing,” 瑕 “fault,” and 胡/何 “what/why”; it gives 廣韻 古疋切. This supports a graphic and phonetic account for 叚, but the bronze-form description is the source’s analysis, not a visually inspected glyph in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 田炜, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心 article reprinted by Sohu
evidence.text: The author reports that pre-Qin excavated texts contain 叚 but not 假, and that 假 first appears in Qin-period documents. He discusses a dated Liye document from Qin Shihuang year 26 (221 BCE): in the author’s reading, 叚 marks lending/giving out while 假 marks borrowing/obtaining. He proposes 假 was formed by adding semantic 人 to 叚 to distinguish a use of the word, while noting that Shuowen and Duan Yucai explain the relationship differently and do not explicitly explain why 人 marks “false.” This is a scholarly proposal, not an uncontested account of character formation.
evidence.title: 〖学闻〗田炜：说“叚”“假”

evidence.source: 田炜, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心 article reprinted by Sohu
evidence.text: The article quotes Shuowen’s analysis of 假 as 从人叚声, “非真也,” and reports Duan Yucai’s view that 假 and 叚 are near-identical in meaning. The author disputes a simple account in which “false” is derived from “borrow,” proposing a graphic differentiation of the written forms instead. The article also notes that later texts no longer consistently maintain the Qin-period 叚/假 distinction; a Han silk manuscript uses 假 for both borrowing and lending. These points separate graphic differentiation from a proposed semantic history.
evidence.title: 〖学闻〗田炜：说“叚”“假”

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學
evidence.field: 叚 entry, lines 157–173: Shuowen, bronze forms, lexical attestations
evidence.text: The entry cites Shuowen’s definition of 叚 as “borrow,” then lists bronze inscription uses read as 嘏 (blessing), 瑕 (fault), 胡 (interrogative), 遐 (interrogative), and a modal reading in 師㝨簋. It does not date each cited inscription on the viewed page. The bronzes establish older graph uses for readings other than 假’s “false” sense, but do not by themselves prove the chronology of semantic development for 假.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學
evidence.text: For 叚, the entry gives 廣韻 page 308 and fanqie 古疋, with Middle Chinese categories 見母, 假攝, 麻韻, 上聲, 開口二等. This is a historical reading for 叚, not evidence on its own for phonetic behavior in 假.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Han character section; its listed sources include Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.field: Glyph origin; phonetic-series and formation data
evidence.text: The page analyzes 假 as ⿰亻叚, a phonosemantic compound, and lists 假 and 叚 in the same 叚 phonetic series. Its Zhengzhang Old Chinese notation gives 假 *kraːʔ / *kraːs and 叚 *kraːʔ. This is a secondary compilation and conflicts in scope with Baxter–Sagart’s two *假 readings; retain each system’s notation rather than combining them.
evidence.title: 假 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese definitions and cited Classical Chinese text
evidence.text: The page proposes a semantic path “borrow” > “simulate” > “deception; false,” and quotes 左傳 僖公五年 for 假道, “borrow a passage.” The cited work is dated there broadly to about the fourth century BCE. This supports an early classical borrowing use in the transmitted text; it does not establish the date of composition or prove that this sense historically preceded the “false” sense.
evidence.title: 假 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry quotes 墨子《經上》 “假，今不然也” as an early textual example of “false / not so”; it also gives examples for borrowing from 左傳 and for acting/temporary office from 韓非子 and 史記. The source supplies texts, not manuscript dates or a securely dated first attestation; do not infer a chronology from its sense list.
evidence.title: 假 jiǎ、jià、xiá - 汉典

evidence.field: 字源字形 and cited senses
evidence.text: The dictionary lists modern senses including false/artificial, borrowing, relying on, granting, and temporary office; the citations include 史記 and 漢書 for false or acting uses and 左傳 for borrowing. These attestations show distinct lexical uses but the page does not establish their relative chronology or a continuous semantic chain.
evidence.title: 假 jiǎ、jià、xiá - 汉典

evidence.text: The entry says 仮 can be a shortened/variant form of 假 in the Japanese-oriented usage described, and also notes 仮 as a variant of 反. This is a nonchronological alternate form, not evidence that 仮 is a historical ancestor of 假 or that Japanese created 假.
evidence.title: [A00203] 假 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: No visually inspected glyph image was used. The available opened CUHK entry provides a scholarly description of 叚’s bronze forms but no readable image was inspected here.

No dated earliest physical attestation for 假 itself was verified. The Qin-period manuscript claim and Qin year 26 example come from the 2021 article’s analysis; the page does not provide direct facsimile inspection in this research.

The proposed semantic bridge “borrow” → “simulate” → “false” is asserted by a secondary dictionary but not independently established by the dated evidence collected. The competing Qin manuscript account treats 人 as a differentiating semantic element and explicitly disputes the simple derivation.

The precise graphic changes from 叚 to 假 through later seal, clerical, and regular scripts were not documented from inspected dated glyph specimens. The article argues for the addition of 人 but detailed paleographic chronology remains open.
The exact official Unihan click-through records for U+5047 and U+53DA failed to load. Local readings are recorded with file/row metadata, but no external Unihan page could be verified for them.
The source record’s Japanese readings, including kari and on readings, were not investigated as evidence for a Japanese-origin history; no such origin is asserted.
Wiktionary’s Tibetan cognate and possible Burmese comparison were not independently researched here; they are not used to support the character’s graphic formation or semantic chronology.
